title: WEST NILE POSITIVE IN CLAY COUNTY
full_story:
Clay County Health Department confirmed the first West Nile virus (WNV) positive mosquito sample of the 2026 season in Clay County.  The positive sample was collected in Louisville on July 24th and was confirmed through routine testing.

Confirmation of a WNV positive mosquito sample means that the virus is circulating in the community and there is a heightened risk of infection for humans.  Residents are urged to take the necessary precautions to protect themselves from mosquito bites.  It is important to remember the three R’s – reduce your exposure to mosquitoes, repel them by wearing insect repellant, and report areas where mosquitoes typically breed.

WNV is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito.  Mosquitoes pick up the virus by feeding on infected birds.  The illness is not spread from person-to-person.  Most people infected with West Nile virus show no symptoms.  However, some people may experience fever, nausea, headache, and muscle aches.  Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.  In rare cases, severe illness including meningitis or encephalitis, or even death, can occur.  People older than 50 are at higher risk for severe illness from West Nile virus.

Because WNV generally appears and spreads in Illinois mosquito populations as early as two to six weeks before it is transmitted to humans, monitoring the mosquito populations in our communities helps us predict when humans will be at risk for WNV infection.  Surveillance activities in Clay County include laboratory tests on mosquito batches and responding to concerns of mosquito production sites.

If you would like more information on West Nile virus, contact the Clay County Health Department at 662-4406 or visit our website www.healthdept.org.

title: HEAVY RAINFALL OVERNIGHT
full_story:
Heavy rainfall overnight caused the National Weather service to issue a Flash Flood Warning for Southern Clay County which expired at 6 this morning.  Because doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area with the heaviest amounts just north and east of Flora.

Steve Lewis with Clay County ESDA reported early this morning that he had no reports of damage from the storms.  There were some scattered power outages.  Here at the US Weather Bureau Station at WNOI we picked up 2.82″ inches of rain overnight.  In the Effingham area 5.5″ of rain was recorded at around 3 this morning.

A funnel cloud was reported near Mt. Erie late last night, but no touch down was reported.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT DOWN
full_story:
Unemployment in Clay County was down a tenth of a percent in June to 4%.  The number of unemployed was up by 1 person from May to 238.  The number of employed jumped 130 to 5,673.  The unemployment rate is down a half of a percent from a year ago.

Jasper County has the lowest unemployment rate in the region at 3.2%, down one tenth of a percent from May.  Effingham County’s unemployment increased a tenth of a percent to 3.4%.  The highest rates in our area are in Fayette, Marion and Wayne Counties, with both Fayette and Marion Counties rate at 4.7% and Wayne County at 4.8%.

In the Centralia-Mt. Vernon market area, there are 600 fewer jobs than a year ago.  The biggest increases were in private education-health services up 525 jobs and government up 100 jobs.  The biggest declines were in trade-transportation-utilities down 350 jobs, professional-business services down 250 jobs, leisure-hospitality down 150, financial activities and manufacturing down 125 jobs apiece and construction down 25 jobs.

title: EFFINGHAM MAN SENTENCED
full_story:
An Effingham man arrested after he barricaded himself in a residence in Effingham has been sentenced to prison.

39-year-old William R. Allen of Effingham barricaded himself in the 200 block of North 4th Street in June.  The incident was related to an assault involving a machete.

One victim was discovered with minor injuries, and one minor was located on the main floor, but officers entered the residence and were able to take the minor to safety.

Allen eventually surrendered to police officers including a Special Response Team without incident.

In court, Allen pleaded guilty to a count of aggravated battery involving use of a deadly weapon.  He was sentenced to three years in prison.  Once out of prison, he will complete six months of supervised release.

title: SHOTS FIRED
full_story:
At 1:50am Friday, Effingham Police Department officers responded to a report of shots fired outside a residence in the 300 block of North 3rd Street.  Upon arriving at the scene, officers learned the occupants of the targeted vehicle were at the Effingham Police Department.

Officers on scene located evidence indicating that a single round from a handgun was fired at a vehicle occupied by one adult and two teenaged juveniles.  None of the occupants were struck during the incident.

In custody in connection with the incident is 18-year-old Jalen N. Herschberger of Effingham.  Herschberger is being held on counts of aggravated discharge of a firearm and unlawful possession of a weapon.  Judge Ericka Sanders ordered Herschberger held in custody pending the filing of formal charges and a detention hearing scheduled for this morning.  The hearing will be held to determine whether continued pretrial detention is warranted under the Illinois Pretrial Fairness Act.

The aggravated discharge of a firearm is a Class 1 felony, meaning possible prison time if Herschberger is found guilty of the offense.  She could face 4 to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to $25,000.

During this incident, Effingham Police were assisted by the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office as well as Illinois State Police Troopers.

title: US ATTORNEY ANNOUNCES VICTORY
full_story:
United States Attorney Steven D. Weinhoeft announced that the United States District Court for the Southern District of Illinois ruled in favor of the United States in its lawsuit against the State of Illinois, Governor J.B. Pritzker, and multiple state entities.

The Court denied the State’s motion to dismiss and granted the United States’ cross-motion for summary judgment, declaring that Illinois’ in-state tuition rules for public universities and community colleges, the RISE Act, and the Illinois DREAM Act are “unconstitutional and invalid” under the Supremacy Clause as applied to aliens not lawfully present.

Weinhoeft says the State of Illinois sought to incentivize illegal immigration on the taxpayer’s dime by treating illegal aliens better than US citizens living in other states, in clear violation of federal law.  He says this ruling enforces the statute Congress wrote and stops the State from putting illegal aliens ahead of American citizens.

Weinhoeft says the federal law is clear a state may not grant postsecondary education benefits to illegal aliens on the basis of residence in that state unless it makes the exact same benefit available to every United States citizen and national, without regard to where they live.  Illinois chose to give preferential treatment based on residence to people here illegally.  It did not extend that same treatment to American citizens who live outside Illinois.  That preference is illegal.

In September 2025, the Department of Justice filed suit to stop these policies.  The Court held oral argument on May 5th.  It has now permanently enjoined the State and the named university and college boards from enforcing the challenged provisions against aliens not lawfully present.  The injunction is stayed for 14 days to permit the defendants to seek a stay pending appeal.

The case was brought by the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Illinois and the US Department of Justice’s Civil Division.
